newsitem.title: UK: London gold turnover down in March vs Feb-LBMA.
newsitem.headline: London gold turnover down in March vs Feb-LBMA.

text.p: Daily gold clearance turnover in the London market in March averaged 36.3 million ounces, down from 40.3 million in February and 37.2 million in January, according to figures from the London Bullion Market Association (LBMA).
But the March turnover was well above the levels prevailing in the last three months of 1996, LBMA said on Monday. In December the gold clearance turnover had averaged 29.8 million ounces.

"The fact that they are a bit down on January and February is what we were expecting. My members in the market say that March was a rather quiet month compared with pretty volatile trading in January and February," said Chris Elston, chief executive of LBMA.
He explained that selling pressure in January and February, including from some central banks, appeared to have come to a halt in March.
The London gold fixing price fell throughout March, from $362.15 on March 3 to $346.05 on March 26 picking up slightly afterwards.
The value of gold cleared in London averaged $12.8 billion versus $14.0 billion in February. Transactions averaged 1,365 daily from 1,378, said the LBMA.
Silver clearance turnover averaged 284.1 million ounces versus 275.0 million in February with average daily value of $1.50 billion from $1.40 billion and on 562 transactions versus 565.
